My understanding is that search engagement and usage is higher than ever. The issue is they are still perfecting the monetization of search ads with gemini. This happened to google previously with introduction of smart phones. Where people thought click through on mobile would kill search revenue. In what world does Google not perfect its monetization of its flagship ai? Zero as far as im concerned.

I think it’s very dubious that they cited FX as the single largest contributor to search deceleration, but they chose not to give the constant currency growth rate.  If FX was really as big of a factor as they claim, they should’ve provided the exact number imho.  Some of the comments about tough comps vs. the World Cup quarter also don’t hold a ton of water when we saw METAs ad business seemingly unaffected by this…

Additionally, I don’t doubt that AI advertising monetization will eventually improve, but it really doesn’t matter much if that growth is largely cannibalisation of search.  Especially since Google is a monopoly in search, but far from it in AI.  Cloud is also a much more commodity/competitive business than Search (never mind the fact that it’s largely driven by a couple of AI labs losing tons of money, and *might* be an outright bubble).  Long run, at the very least, I think all of this is bad news long run for margins, even if revenue growth rebounds.
